root_cause.text: `wait_sb_inodes()` in `fs/fs-writeback.c` treated all superblock inodes as requiring writeback completion, but FUSE writeback-cache mappings lacked an `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` marker so sync/wait logic could block forever on inodes that do not provide persistence guarantees.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `mapping_no_data_integrity(mapping)` to the `wait_sb_inodes()` skip condition and documents that such mappings “there's no need to wait for the writeout to complete”; it also sets `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` for FUSE writeback-cache in `fuse_init_file_inode()`, and the commit message says this fixes a regression where a faulty FUSE server that never replies causes `wait_sb_inodes()` to wait forever.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip waiting for inode writeback when the mapping lacks data integrity semantics.
intent_record.what: The condition in wait_sb_inodes() was changed from skipping only when a mapping is not tagged for PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK to skipping when the mapping is either not writeback-tagged or has mapping_no_data_integrity() set. A comment was added explaining that mappings without data integrity semantics do not need writeout completion waiting.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the loop will no longer wait for writeback completion on inodes whose address_space lacks data integrity semantics, even if they are still writeback-tagged. This reduces unnecessary waiting for writeback that cannot guarantee persistent storage semantics, while preserving the existing behavior for mappings that do provide data integrity.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark FUSE writeback-cache file mappings as lacking data integrity guarantees in addition to the existing reclaim deadlock hint.
intent_record.what: The conditional block in fuse_init_file_inode() was expanded from a single call under `if (fc->writeback_cache)` to a braced block that now calls both `mapping_set_writeback_may_deadlock_on_reclaim(&inode->i_data)` and `mapping_set_no_data_integrity(&inode->i_data)` when writeback cache is enabled.
intent_record.how: When FUSE writeback caching is active, the inode mapping is now additionally marked as not providing data integrity guarantees. This changes the filesystem mapping flags used by the kernel and can alter how upper layers treat cached file data, preventing incorrect assumptions about integrity semantics.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new mapping flag to represent address spaces without data integrity guarantees.
intent_record.what: An enum value named AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY was added to enum mapping_flags with value 11 and the comment "no data integrity guarantees".
intent_record.how: This introduces a new mapping flag that can be used by code to mark an address_space mapping as not providing data integrity guarantees, enabling later logic to distinguish such mappings from normal ones.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add helper APIs to set and test the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY address_space flag.
intent_record.what: Two new static inline helper functions were added to the address_space flag helpers: mapping_set_no_data_integrity(struct address_space *mapping), which sets the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY bit in mapping->flags, and mapping_no_data_integrity(const struct address_space *mapping), which returns whether that bit is set.
intent_record.how: This exposes a standardized way for callers to mark and query an address_space as not requiring data integrity handling. At runtime, code can now explicitly record and check this state via these helpers instead of manipulating the flag directly.

vuln_statements.explanation: This wait condition only skips inode writeback when the mapping has no writeback tags. Because it did not also recognize mappings lacking data integrity guarantees, wait_sb_inodes() could continue waiting on FUSE writeback-cache inodes indefinitely.

This is the pre-fix marker applied to FUSE writeback-cache mappings, but it did not set the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY-style semantics needed by sync/wait logic. As a result, the mapping was treated like a normal persistent mapping and could cause indefinite waiting.
